reports.title: Wynn Resorts, Limited Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results

desk.headline: Revenue down 8% to $1.69bn and adjusted EPS $0.33 vs $0.58 expected, miss; Las Vegas hit by low table hold; no guidance
results: Operating revenue fell 8% to $1.69bn; all four properties sold less than a year ago, led by Wynn Palace (-$51.7m) and Las Vegas (-$45.8m).
Net income to shareholders dropped to $17.3m ($0.17 a share) from $88.3m; adjusted EPS was $0.33 vs $0.86.
Adjusted Property EBITDAR fell 19% to $464.2m; Las Vegas was weakest (-22%) as table hold of 18.9% came in below its normal range.
Encore Boston Harbor EBITDAR fell 14% to $50.1m during a strike that began in early September; Macau VIP hold ran above normal at both properties.
Bought back $58.1m of shares ($268.0m authority left), declared a $0.25 dividend, and refinanced $900m of 2027 notes with 2035 notes at 6.875%.

guidance.summary: Wynn gives no revenue or earnings guidance. The release only repeats that Wynn Al Marjan Island in the UAE is expected to open in September 2027.

points: CEO Craig Billings called it a quarter with "more headwinds than tailwinds".
Las Vegas room rates and RevPAR were up about 3% y/y and kept rising in October; Formula 1 weekend and 2027 group bookings are pacing ahead of prior years.
A framework deal with Boston unions was reached on call day and ratified that evening; terms were not disclosed and cost impact not yet quantified.
As reported, low Las Vegas hold cost about $24m, while Macau September was soft and October volumes faded late in the month.
As reported, the UAE project remains on track for September 2027 with remaining equity needs of $465-590m.
call.source: Call coverage: Hotel Dive, 6 Nov 2026; Earnings Whispers, 5 Nov 2026 (no prepared remarks filed)

watch: Whether Las Vegas hold normalises and October strength carries through the fourth quarter.
Cost of the new Encore Boston Harbor labour agreement.
Macau mass-market demand and progress toward the September 2027 UAE opening.
